_why: 2026-10-25, THE AWS EDITION. Three changes to the draft below, each from a decision made that day:
* agent-bait scanning is REMOVED. It is a capability of the MCP proxy firewall, a different product,
and its dimension was never on this rate card, so advertising it would promise something AWS cannot bill.
* '13 tools' is GONE. The AWS-hosted MCP endpoint serves the five tools this listing sells plus status
(RS_MCP_TOOLS), so the copy says 'an MCP server' and no count.
* 'newly-registered' is GONE from the MCP registry sentence: the registration-age lookup is an outside
call and does not run for AWS-licensed keys. The copy now claims only what the endpoint does there.
And one claim was ADDED, which is a promise the code must keep: 'the queries you send are not forwarded to
outside data providers'. That is why CLAUDE.md carries the rule about new lookups on these endpoints.
The draft ShortDescription was 631 characters. The live, AWS-accepted one is 475 and the field's limit is
500, so the draft would have been refused. This one is checked by test_bundle_d_listing_copy.py.
THE FIELDS THIS FILE OVERRIDES ON THE LIVE LISTING, and nothing else.
tools/marketplace_add_dimension.py --with-copy reads the LIVE entity, applies
these keys over it, and sends the whole information block back. It is a
partial on purpose: UpdateInformation REPLACES everything, so the only safe
way to change three fields is to round-trip the other six from a fresh
capture rather than retype them here and get one subtly wrong.
TWO THINGS CHANGED, 2026-09-09, and the first is a correction on a PUBLIC
page a competitor can read.
1. THE CORPUS COUNTS ARE GONE. The live listing said '5.0M+ indicators of
compromise, 3,750+ malware families, and 85+ monitored criminal Telegram
marketplaces' in three places. MEASUREMENT DOCTRINE has said since August
that the corpus headline is never quoted, because most of it is ingested
public feeds every target buyer already has, and quoting it nearly killed
the Segment 1 outreach in front of people who checked. The listing was the
most public place we were still doing it.
REPLACING THOSE NUMBERS WITH FRESHER NUMBERS WAS THE WRONG FIX, and it was
the first thing this session proposed. Corrected figures go stale on the
same schedule the old ones did, and each refresh is an AWS change set with
their review latency attached. So the copy now names the SOURCES, which do
not change, instead of counts, which change hourly. A listing should carry
only claims that stay true without maintenance.
2. THIRTEEN TOOLS, WHICH IS A NUMBER THAT HOLDS. It changes when we ship a
tool, which is a deliberate act with a commit behind it, not a background
process. Counted from hf-space-mcp-server/app.py's own manifest, which is
the file deployed as this listing's registered MCP endpoint. Verify before
any resubmission:
grep -c '"name": "' hf-space-mcp-server/app.py
agent-bait scanning is named because this change set adds its dimension.
Sending the copy without the dimension would advertise something the rate
card cannot bill.
FIELD COUNTS ARE HELD AT WHAT AWS HAS ALREADY ACCEPTED, NOT AT WHAT WOULD
READ BEST. A first draft carried four Highlights and fifteen SearchKeywords.
The live listing carries three and thirteen, and the UpdateInformation change
in aws_marketplace/bundle_a_create_entity.json -- a change set AWS actually
accepted -- carries three Highlights too. AWS documents a maximum of three.
A rejected change set is not a free retry: it costs a full review cycle on a
PUBLISHED listing, and this submission is carrying the agent-bait dimension
with it. So the fourth highlight was folded into the third rather than
gambled, and the two new keywords displaced two weaker ones instead of
growing the list. Room to be right is worth more than room to be complete.
ShortDescription: RelayShield's Consumption Security API Bundles deliver metered access to focused threat intelligence and identity risk detection capabilities, billed entirely through AWS Marketplace. Bundle D, Agentic Attack Surface, covers MCP registry risk, prompt-injection breach correlation, agent-framework CVE targeting, bulk per-agent identity risk scoring and LLM credential exposure detection, scored from RelayShield's own corpus. Callable by AI agents over MCP and by REST.
LongDescription:
Bundle D: Agentic Attack Surface is built for the emerging risk of AI-agent-driven attacks. It includes MCP registry risk scoring (detecting typosquatted AI agent tool servers and domains already known to be malicious), prompt-injection breach correlation (surfacing exposed sessions tied to prompt-injection attacks via infostealer log analysis), agent-framework CVE targeting risk (CVE exposure scoped to your declared agent stack, LangChain, AutoGPT, CrewAI, and similar), bulk per-agent identity risk scoring across up to 10 domains and 5 agents each, purpose-built for AI governance programs and MSP client sweeps, and LLM credential exposure detection to detect exposed LLM/AI provider API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, xAI, Replicate) in criminal stealer logs.

The checks are delivered as an MCP server, so an AI agent can call them directly as part of its own reasoning, and as REST endpoints for existing security pipelines.

Every score is computed from RelayShield's own continuously collected corpus: monitored criminal Telegram marketplaces, infostealer log dumps, and public indicator feeds. The queries you send are not forwarded to outside data providers, and every response names any signal it did not run, so a missing signal is never mistaken for a clean result. We deliberately do not quote a corpus headline here. A total indicator count is dominated by public feeds that most buyers already ingest, and it is out of date the week it is published; what matters is the exclusive fraction, which we report per capability on request.

Billing note: the monthly minimum commitment applies whether or not you call a given security function that month, and per-Unit charges apply only to the functions you actually call above the included baseline. Your API key is issued automatically by email when your AWS Marketplace subscription activates, with full usage instructions included. All access is provisioned and billed through AWS Marketplace.
Highlights: Each bundle is licensed independently through AWS Marketplace, with no dependency on any other bundle or platform-wide subscription.
Contract-with-consumption pricing: a minimum monthly commitment covers included usage, with transparent per-call pricing for anything above that baseline.
Scored from RelayShield's own continuously collected corpus, with no customer query sent to outside data providers, and callable directly by an AI agent over MCP.
